rule.description: A bundled example image translation unit defines part of the shared bring-up self-report (appfw) mechanism itself: an appfw_* function definition or file-scope non-const appfw_* protocol state written directly in the image. The mechanism is a bundle-wide responsibility; whatever an image defines privately is a copy that every protocol change must touch again. Per-image const identity data, per-device/per-core selection macros, function-local statics, and definitions pulled in from headers or a shared module are exempt.

checks.description: Detect private per-image copies of the shared bring-up self-report mechanism: appfw_* function definitions and file-scope non-const appfw_* protocol state written directly inside a bundled example image translation unit.
checks.detected_relation: example image TU -> direct definition of a piece of the bundle-wide bring-up self-report mechanism (this image now owns a copy that all images were supposed to share)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The bring-up self-report is one responsibility of the example bundle, but each credited location implements it privately next to its own main(): an externally identical protocol surface (progress marker, stage advance, banner layout, bundle revision) is re-created file by file, so one conceptual protocol change requires the same edit in every image. Each entry is one image whose copy must be dissolved; a match remains wherever any part of the mechanism is still defined in the image.

excluded.what: Per-image const identity data inside the example TUs
excluded.reason: Image name, board(s), core and revision digits are genuinely each image's own data. They are const-qualified records (or preprocessor macros, which never reach the AST) and are intentionally exempt from the shared-mechanism rule; after consolidation they are exactly what should stay inside each image.

excluded.what: Function-local statics inside the match-crediting definitions
excluded.locations: the per-image banner buffers declared inside appfw_signature in each TU
excluded.reason: Local static scratch buffers are not file-scope protocol state; only the mechanically shared protocol surface (state variable, entry points) defines the ownership being credited.

excluded.what: Definitions reached from headers or a shared module
excluded.locations: appfw definitions reached from a header or shared module (e.g. a consolidated examples/common/appfw.h + appfw.c in a repaired layout); SDK headers during parsing
excluded.reason: Only what the example image TU itself defines is credited. A shared module compiled into every image is the wanted shape (one home for the mechanism), not a scattered private copy; header definitions are not written 'directly here' by the image.
Build wiring, not firmware image translation units; the rule is an AST rule over C/C++ sources and the scripts neither define nor re-home the mechanism.

excluded.locations: tests/ integration projects, cmake/ modules, STM32 CMSIS/HAL/FreeRTOS fetched SDK sources
excluded.reason: Outside the example-image boundary of the bundled bring-up protocol; not smuggled into coverage under this rule.

excluded.locations: the firmware entry point of each analyzed example image TU, for each of the 21 device configurations the example build systems compile
excluded.reason: An anchor diagnostic per (TU, device configuration) is required for the run to count as reliable; it proves the TU parsed past its device-dependent conditionals and is not used to credit or count matches.
